baseline_rationale: Based on historical data and trends in global health, the likelihood of new Public Health Emergencies of International Concern (PHEICs) being declared can vary. Given the ongoing challenges with emerging infectious diseases, a probability of 40% for no new PHEICs seems reasonable, as many outbreaks can be contained or managed without escalating to a PHEIC. A 30% chance for one new PHEIC reflects the possibility of a significant outbreak occurring, while another 30% for two or more new PHEICs acknowledges the unpredictable nature of global health threats, especially in a post-pandemic world.
